Forum sites like this, utilize a voting system to establish relevancy with the community for not just submissions, but also comments. This gives the opportunity for the community to act as a filter on an individual basis and allows for a "community majority rules" atmosphere which some complain can lead to the development of a "hive mind".

The beauty of this site is the ability to branch out and create separate areas for users with like views or interests so that they may discuss or share content without worrying about appeasing the entire site, and instead communicating with like minded users. In a perfect version of this system users would respectfully post according to the area they were in and their bolder comments or submissions would be saved for areas they would find common interests or support.

However, it is more common you'll find users branching out unpopular postings, or ideas, into subs filled with other users who may not agree with them. Now we've grown a debate on this, where some users call for more "civil" discourse, and often times the loudest cries get the attention and newer rules added regardless of the voice of the many.

In many scenarios recently the voting patterns have consistently shown a disdain for bad moderation, bad enforcement of rules, trolling, adding new rules. In all of these situations the votes reflected a community standing in agreement, and in almost all of those situations some very loud trolls got their way by labeling the down vote patterns as "brigades" and blaming them on one sub. That sub rarely has a post reach 50 up votes, yet these trolls would have you believe they are responsible for tens of thousands of down votes over the last couple months.

Voting is much more important than most power moderators would want you to know. When a post gets hundreds of positive or negative votes it becomes an indicator on content, and on the community's wants. Moderators would be keen to paying more attention to those very votes, than the substance of the comments in their subs. If 12 to 20 users all seem to be complaining about the same thing, but literally thousands of votes reflect a different opinion then you should act on the will of the thousands, not the few squawking users. I'd ask all of you as users to be more active in holding your moderators accountable to keeping you as users happy. For far too long the attitude of moderators has shifted away from serving their users, to the point where often times you're told to leave if you don't like the sub you may have known as a home away from home for months. This is unacceptable, and only with our votes will we show how against this we are.

Down votes are a necessary part of culling toxicity and nonsense, don't fall for the "harassment, brigade, or victim" game each time and instead determine for yourself why someone might down vote that user. Don't get sucked into letting other users tell you how to down vote, it's your 1 vote in each situation to use how you see fit, so go for it.
Down voting is an important process for filtering content on voat because it gives individual users the chance to affirm content they enjoy, and reject content they dislike

To me, that sounds like some reddit minded score keeping. Here, I feel a no-voat is equivalent to a reddit downvoat, and the downies are reserved for content that is off topic or otherwise misposted. The purp arrow should not be a disagree button, but an indicator of irrelevant or immaterial content and conversation. To me the no-voat is the disagree button, and the blue voat is the agree button. If you feel you must use the purp arrow, at least try leave a comment to explain to the poster why you felt their content was not worth being seen by the rest of voat.
